The Politics of Death in Porfirian México: The State Funeral as a Rite of Reconciliation, 1876–1890
This dissertation examines the state funeral in Porfirian Mexican society as a political ritual that helped consolidate the power of the Díaz regime.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Porfiriato’s state funeral rituals were a form of public policy that helped to shape the political culture in which Mexicans lived.

the Porfirian state was able to successfully manage the political and symbolic dimensions of death in order to consolidate its authority in the face of the challenges of a rapidly urbanizing and industrializing society.
